events.title: Ratification of the 19th Amendment
events.description: Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the 19th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, narrowly passing the House vote after a tie-breaking switch by young legislator Harry T. Burn, who was influenced by a letter from his mother. The amendment was certified as part of the Constitution on August 26, 1920.
events.significance: Secured the constitutional right of American women to vote, marking a landmark victory for the women's suffrage movement.

events.title: James Meredith Graduates from the University of Mississippi
events.description: James Meredith, who had integrated the University of Mississippi in 1962 amid violent riots and federal intervention, graduated with a degree in political science, becoming the first African American to graduate from the university.
events.significance: His graduation was a milestone in the desegregation of American higher education and the broader civil rights movement.

events.title: Death of Genghis Khan
events.description: Genghis Khan, founder and first Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, died during a campaign against the Western Xia dynasty. The exact cause of death remains debated, and his burial place is unknown. Dates vary by source, but August 18, 1227 is commonly cited.
events.significance: His death marked the end of the founding era of the Mongol Empire, which his successors expanded into the largest contiguous land empire in history.

events.title: Disappearance of the Roanoke Colony Discovered
events.description: English governor John White returned to Roanoke Island after a three-year absence caused by the Anglo-Spanish War, and found the settlement deserted, with only the word 'CROATOAN' carved into a post. His granddaughter Virginia Dare, born in 1587, was the first English child born in the Americas.
events.significance: The mystery of the 'Lost Colony' became one of the most enduring puzzles of early American colonial history.

events.title: Discovery of Helium
events.description: French astronomer Pierre Janssen observed a new yellow spectral line in the Sun's chromosphere during a total solar eclipse in India on August 18, 1868. The line was later attributed to a new element named helium by Norman Lockyer and Edward Frankland.
events.significance: Helium was the first element discovered in space before being found on Earth, advancing the field of astrophysics and spectroscopy.
